review_comments: [team convention] Round money only with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent). Python's round() and a bare Decimal.quantize() use banker's rounding and give wrong invoice totals.

item.title: Round money with the project's round_money helper
item.description: Monetary results must be rounded via ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent), not Python round() or bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding.
item.content: Before returning any computed money value, wrap it in round_money(...). Check the repo's money module for existing helpers (round_money, to_money, ZERO) and reuse them rather than inventing rounding logic.

item.title: Read existing sibling functions for conventions
item.description: The invoice module already had line_total and invoice_total showing the exact pattern: to_money(...) for inputs, round_money(...) for outputs, ZERO as sum seed.
item.content: When adding a function to a module, inspect neighboring functions first; mirroring their conversion/rounding idioms satisfies hidden conventions and review comments.

item.title: Handle empty/zero-denominator cases explicitly
item.description: Guard division by total quantity and return ZERO for invoices without lines, as the spec requires.
item.content: Compute the denominator first, return ZERO (the project constant) when it is falsy, then perform the weighted sum and round the quotient.
